about: Requirements the Sherpa raises for teams outside this newsroom, each with its evidence. Requirements for this newsroom's own members are generated from the friction log and go to the conductor.

items.title: Never print a vault key on the receiving side
items.what: When an agent opens a sealed message whose text carries a vault key (the editor's 'A message I write' route in recipe 1), `pki-agent open` prints the whole text, key included, to standard output, which an agent's transcript keeps. `--save` writes only attached files, so it saves nothing for a key sent as text. The handover rules say a vault key is never printed; the tool makes that the agent's job.
items.evidence: The Sherpa's own handover of the collaborators vault's key, 23 October 2026: the key reached the transcript only as '<redacted>' because the Sherpa filtered the output itself.
items.proposal: In `open`, detect a vault-key shape in the text and never print it: write it to a file (0600) beside `--save`, or refuse without `--save`; and in the browser's recipe 1, carry a vault key as a file, never as message text.

items.title: Say on handover.md how a receiving agent stores the key
items.what: Section B says to store a key 'in the vault of vaults'; an agent that only needs to read one vault has none, and is left to choose where to keep the key.
items.proposal: One line for a session agent: keep it in a 0600 file outside any repository, feed it to `sgit clone -` on standard input, delete it at the end of the session.
